When a listing catches your eye, what's the first number you check before you ring the agent?

hits.name: levelsio
hits.hook: 'Everything I do runs on my VPS servers. The only interface is Termius SSH and then Claude Code.' Whole-life stack in one post; 558 bookmarks.
hits.draft_en:
Running everything on one VPS is a great setup right up until the VPS is gone.

Three questions worth asking before that day:

Where's the copy?
Is it with a different provider?
When did you last restore it somewhere else?

Nearly 30 years in disaster recovery and the third one is the one people skip.
hits.video_tip: 30-45s talking head at your desk: say the opening line, then put each of the three questions on screen as you ask it. Hold on the third one for two seconds before you cut.

hits.name: Arvid Kahl
hits.hook: A fork of a private repo got cascade-deleted when the original went, and that was 'expected behavior'. Audit-trail lesson; 42 replies.
hits.draft_en:
A fork of a private repo got deleted because the original was deleted. Apparently that's expected behaviour.

Good test for any copy you rely on: if the original disappears, does the copy go with it?

If yes, it's a mirror, not a backup.

Forks, same-account snapshots, replicas that sync deletes. Same trap.
hits.video_tip: 15-20s screen recording: show a repo list, then a mock fork disappearing when the original is deleted (a test account only). End on the line 'mirror, not a backup' in big text.

narrative_synthesis: levelsio carried the day again: a sombre train-safety stat went huge, but the builder posts that got saved were his Omarchy unboxing and 'everything runs on my VPS with Claude Code over SSH'. Open questions (organic chicken, Product Hunt's X login) pulled the most replies per view. Arvid pushed MCP with a real adoption chart and flagged a fork that vanished with its original. Nobody asked what happens when the one VPS or the original repo is gone, which is Nick's disaster recovery lane.
